overview: The City Council referred a major zoning amendment for the Mystic Avenue corridor to the Community Development Board and approved a new collective bargaining agreement for the parking union. Residents also presented a petition and significant testimony expressing concern over the potential loss of Senior Center parking due to proposed redevelopment in Medford Square.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognition and Meeting Records
items.summary: Council thanked DPW employees Jeff Gange and Anthony Pompeo for an act of kindness and approved the records of October 15, 2024.

items.title: Committee Reports
items.summary: Council approved committee reports concerning upcoming ballot questions, public health initiatives, Human Rights Commission updates, and the Mystic Avenue Valley District zoning draft.

items.title: Senior Center Parking Petition
items.summary: Resident Marian Tomaszczuk presented a petition signed by seniors concerned that a Request for Proposals for redevelopment behind City Hall would eliminate vital parking for the Senior Center. The administration stated that the RFP requires developers to replace the parking, though residents expressed skepticism regarding accessibility during and after construction.

items.title: HERO Act Local Options
items.summary: Council tabled a resolution to adopt local veteran property tax exemptions under the HERO Act pending financial impact analysis and legal review.

items.title: Fire Department Policy Review
items.summary: Approved an amended resolution requesting the final consultant report on fire department policies and inviting the consultant to a future meeting to discuss their findings.

items.title: Mystic Avenue Corridor District Rezoning
items.summary: Council referred the proposed zoning ordinance for the Mystic Avenue Corridor District to the Community Development Board for a mandatory public hearing. The proposal seeks to create a mixed-use district to increase commercial revenue and housing growth while maintaining buffers for residential areas.

items.title: Parking Union Collective Bargaining Agreement
items.summary: Council approved and ordained a collective bargaining agreement for the parking union covering fiscal years 2023 through 2027.

items.title: Community Preservation Committee Appointment
items.summary: Approved the appointment of Maisha Majumder to the Community Preservation Committee for a term expiring in September 2025.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Appropriations
items.summary: Tabled funding requests for fire engine repairs, cemetery soil removal, grant matching, and City Hall window restoration until the next regular meeting.

items.title: Paper Street Rights Transfer
items.summary: Approved the transfer and acquisition of rights in a paper street near Dexter Street to facilitate the repair of a collapsed retaining wall on private property.
